correctness.rationale: The claim has fixed finite input data and was reconstructed from definitions. The verifier obtains 32 facets, 188 nonempty faces, an acyclic 91-pair Morse matching with critical-cell counts 1,1,4 in dimensions 0,3,4, exact rational boundary ranks 7,21,35,28, and Betti vector 1,0,0,1,4. Forman discrete Morse theory reduces the space to one 0-cell, one 3-cell and four 4-cells; rank zero of the cellular 4-to-3 boundary forces all attaching degrees to vanish, and degree classifies maps \(S^3\to S^3\), yielding the stated wedge. Nonshellability follows from nonzero H_3 in a pure 4-complex. Minimality is both implied by Bayer et al. Corollary 5.5 after checking cube 3-connectivity/3-regularity and exhaustively verified by shelling all 255 proper induced-subgraph cut complexes.

value.rationale: The result answers the defining literature's explicit program of identifying induced-minimal nonshellable cut-complex graphs with a canonical 3-connected graph. The cube is a natural first three-dimensional grid, and its cut complex exhibits mixed adjacent-dimensional homology and a concrete wedge \(S^3\) with four \(S^4\) summands, sharply contrasting shellable rectangular-grid cases. The exact homotopy type and minimal obstruction are structural facts, not a parameter tweak or arbitrary finite slice.
